title: Ancient Indian History
summary: From the Harappan cities to the Cholas: sites and finds, Vedic texts, Buddhism & Jainism, Mauryas, Guptas, Harsha and the southern dynasties. SSC asks 1–2 direct fact questions per shift — mostly pairings (site–find, council–king, book–author, dynasty–capital), so tables and mnemonics give quick marks.

subtopics.title: Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilisation
subtopics.concept:
**Basics you must know**

| Point | Fact |
|---|---|
| Age | Bronze Age (copper + tin); **no iron** |
| Mature phase | c. 2600–1900 BCE (NCERT) |
| First site excavated | **Harappa, 1921** (Daya Ram Sahni) — hence "Harappan civilisation" |
| ASI Director-General then | **Sir John Marshall** (announced the discovery in 1924) |
| Script | Pictographic, written right to left (boustrophedon in places); **still undeciphered** |
| Seals | Mostly **steatite**; most common animal motif = **unicorn** (one-horned bull) |
| Religion | Mother Goddess, "Pashupati" (proto-Shiva) seal, pipal tree, phallic stones; **no temples found** |
| Crops | Wheat, barley, peas, sesame; **cotton first grown here** (Greeks later called it *Sindon*); rice husk at **Lothal & Rangpur** |
| Town plan | Grid pattern, covered drains, burnt bricks (ratio 1:2:4), citadel (west) + lower town (east) |

**Site table (most asked)**

| Site | River | Present location | Excavator (year) | Signature finds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Harappa** | Ravi | Sahiwal (Montgomery) dist., Punjab, **Pakistan** | Daya Ram Sahni (1921) | Rows of granaries, red-sandstone male torso, Cemetery R-37 & H, coffin burial |
| **Mohenjo-daro** ("mound of the dead") | Indus | Larkana dist., Sindh, **Pakistan** | R.D. Banerji (1922) | **Great Bath**, Great Granary, bronze **Dancing Girl**, steatite **bearded priest**, Pashupati seal, assembly hall |
| **Chanhudaro** | Indus | Sindh, Pakistan | N.G. Majumdar (1931) | **Bead-making** workshop; the only city **without a citadel** |
| **Lothal** | Bhogava (near Sabarmati) | Ahmedabad dist., **Gujarat** | S.R. Rao (1954–55) | **Dockyard**, rice husk, fire altars, Persian Gulf seal, double burial |
| **Kalibangan** ("black bangles") | Ghaggar | Hanumangarh dist., **Rajasthan** | A. Ghosh (found 1953); B.B. Lal & B.K. Thapar (dug 1960s) | **Ploughed field**, fire altars, camel bones |
| **Banawali** | Ghaggar (Saraswati) | Fatehabad dist., **Haryana** | R.S. Bisht (1973–74) | Clay **plough model**, barley |
| **Dholavira** | Between Mansar & Manhar streams | Khadir Bet, Kutch, **Gujarat** | J.P. Joshi (found 1967–68); R.S. Bisht (dug 1990) | **Water reservoirs/conservation**, three-part city, **10-letter signboard**; UNESCO site (2021) |
| **Rakhigarhi** | Ghaggar plain | Hisar dist., **Haryana** | Amarendra Nath (1997–2000) | **Largest Harappan site in India**; ancient DNA study |
| **Surkotada** | — | Kutch, Gujarat | J.P. Joshi (1964) | Horse remains (bones) |
| **Ropar (Rupnagar)** | Sutlej | **Punjab (India)** | Y.D. Sharma (1953–55) | First site dug after Independence; dog buried with man |
| **Alamgirpur** | Hindon | Meerut, **UP** | Y.D. Sharma (1958) | **Easternmost** site |
| **Sutkagendor** | Dasht | Makran coast, Baluchistan (Pak.) | Aurel Stein (1927) | **Westernmost** site; trade post |
| **Manda** | Chenab | Jammu, **J&K** | J.P. Joshi (1982) | **Northernmost** site |
| **Daimabad** | Pravara (Godavari basin) | Ahmednagar dist., **Maharashtra** | — | **Southernmost** site; **bronze chariot** |
| **Kot Diji** | Indus | Sindh, Pakistan | F.A. Khan (1955) | Pre-Harappan fortified settlement |

**States with most sites in India:** Gujarat (Lothal, Dholavira, Surkotada, Rangpur, Rojdi), Haryana (Rakhigarhi, Banawali, Bhirrana), Rajasthan (Kalibangan), Punjab (Ropar), UP (Alamgirpur), Maharashtra (Daimabad).

tricks.title: Four extremes — "Many Donkeys Are Slow"
tricks.body: **M**anda (North, J&K) · **D**aimabad (South, Maharashtra) · **A**lamgirpur (East, UP) · **S**utkagendor (West, Baluchistan).

example.q: The easternmost Harappan site is —
example.solution: Donkeys **A**re → **A**lamgirpur (Meerut, UP) on the Hindon.

tricks.title: Site-to-find pairing
tricks.body: **Lothal = Launch** (dockyard) · **Kali-bangan = Kheti** (ploughed field) · **Mohenjo = Majestic Bath** (Great Bath) · **Chanhu = Chain of beads** (bead factory) · **Dholavira = Drop of water** (reservoirs).

mistakes: Harappa is on the **Ravi**, Mohenjo-daro on the **Indus** — do not swap.
Ploughed **field** = Kalibangan; clay **plough model** = Banawali.
Largest site in India = Rakhigarhi; Mohenjo-daro and Harappa are in Pakistan.
Harappans knew copper/bronze and gold/silver but **not iron**; horse evidence is doubtful (only Surkotada bones).
subtopics.notes:
### A lost civilisation, found twice
Until the 1920s schoolbooks said Indian history began with the Vedic age. Then in **1921** Daya Ram Sahni dug at **Harappa** (on the Ravi, in Punjab, Pakistan) and in **1922** R.D. Banerji dug at **Mohenjo-daro** ("mound of the dead", on the Indus, Sindh). The finds were so alike that Sir John Marshall announced in 1924 a whole new civilisation, older than anything known in India. Because Harappa was dug first, the correct name is the **Harappan civilisation**; "Indus Valley civilisation" is the older popular name. It is a **Bronze Age** culture — copper and tin, but **no iron** — and its mature phase lasted about **2600–1900 BCE**.

### How the cities were built
Every big Harappan city follows the same plan, and that plan is the most-asked exam fact.
- The town is divided into two parts: a raised **citadel** in the **west** (for the rulers, granaries, big public buildings) and the **lower town** in the **east** (where ordinary people lived).
- Streets cut each other at **right angles** — a **grid pattern** — with covered drains along the roads. Every house had its own well and bathroom, and the waste water flowed into street drains through clay pipes.
- Buildings used **burnt bricks** of a fixed ratio **1 : 2 : 4** (width : height : length). Using standard bricks everywhere is the clearest sign of a strong central authority.
- The **Great Bath** of Mohenjo-daro is a public tank with steps on two sides and a bitumen (water-proof) lining; the **Great Granary** stood nearby.

### The site table — one find, one site
Exams test the pairing "site ↔ special find" again and again.

| Site | River / state | Signature find |
|---|---|---|
| Harappa | Ravi (Punjab, Pak.) | Rows of granaries, Cemetery R-37, coffin burial |
| Mohenjo-daro | Indus (Sindh, Pak.) | Great Bath, Great Granary, bronze Dancing Girl, Pashupati seal |
| Chanhudaro | Indus (Sindh) | Bead-making workshop; **no citadel** |
| Lothal | Bhogava (Gujarat) | **Dockyard**, rice husk, fire altars |
| Kalibangan | Ghaggar (Rajasthan) | **Ploughed field**, fire altars |
| Banawali | Ghaggar (Haryana) | Clay **plough model**, barley |
| Dholavira | Kutch (Gujarat) | **Water reservoirs**, 10-letter signboard; UNESCO 2021 |
| Rakhigarhi | Ghaggar (Haryana) | **Largest site in India** |
| Surkotada | Kutch (Gujarat) | Horse bones |
| Ropar | Sutlej (Punjab, India) | First site dug after Independence |
| Alamgirpur | Hindon (UP) | **Easternmost** site |
| Sutkagendor | Dasht (Baluchistan) | **Westernmost** site |
| Manda | Chenab (J&K) | **Northernmost** site |
| Daimabad | Pravara (Maharashtra) | **Southernmost** site; bronze chariot |

The four extremes run north-south-east-west: **Manda, Daimabad, Alamgirpur, Sutkagendor**.

### Economy and daily life
- **Agriculture:** wheat and barley were the staple crops; **cotton** was grown here for the first time in the world (Greeks later called it *sindon*, after Sindh). Rice husks appear at **Lothal and Rangpur** in Gujarat.
- **Trade:** seals of **steatite** (soapstone) with animal motifs — the **unicorn bull** is the commonest — were pressed on clay tags for bales of goods. Trade with Mesopotamia is proved by Persian Gulf and Mesopotamian finds; the **dockyard at Lothal** served sea trade.
- **Metal work:** copper and bronze tools, gold and silver ornaments; the famous **bronze Dancing Girl** of Mohenjo-daro shows lost-wax casting. **Iron was unknown.**

### Religion and society
No temple building has been found anywhere — that is a key difference from Egypt or Mesopotamia. Worship seems to have centred on the **Mother Goddess** figurines, a **proto-Shiva (Pashupati)** seal showing a figure seated cross-legged surrounded by animals, the **pipal** tree, and small stone linga-like objects. Burial was in brick chambers or pits; some graves (Lothal, Kalibangan) show **double burials**. The **script** is pictographic, read right to left (boustrophedon in places), and is **still undeciphered** — so we know the civilisation only through objects, not through its own words.

### Why it declined (standard textbook view)
Around 1900 BCE the cities thinned out. Suggested causes work together, not alone: river shifts, floods, drying of the region, overuse of land. No single cause is proved — exam options usually ask which is **not** a cause (a favourite wrong option is "Aryan invasion, proved by evidence").

### Quick revision
- 1921 Harappa (Daya Ram Sahni); 1922 Mohenjo-daro (R.D. Banerji); announced by John Marshall (1924).
- Bronze Age — **no iron**; burnt bricks 1:2:4; grid streets, covered drains.
- Citadel west + lower town east; Great Bath & Great Granary — Mohenjo-daro.
- Lothal = dockyard + rice; Kalibangan = ploughed field; Dholavira = reservoirs + signboard.
- Extremes: Manda (N), Daimabad (S), Alamgirpur (E), Sutkagendor (W).
- Largest in India: Rakhigarhi (Haryana). Commonest seal motif: unicorn bull.
- No temples; Mother Goddess + Pashupati seal; script undeciphered.

patterns.name: Harappan site ↔ signature find
patterns.howToSpot: The stem names a find — dockyard, Great Bath, ploughed field, bead factory, dancing girl — and asks for the site, or gives a site and asks what was found there.
patterns.logic:
1. Recall the one-find-one-site table (Lothal = dockyard, Kalibangan = ploughed field, Chanhudaro = beads).
2. Beware near-pairs: ploughed **field** is Kalibangan, clay plough **model** is Banawali; Great **Bath** is Mohenjo-daro, rows of **granaries** are Harappa.
3. Eliminate sites whose famous find you already know from the options.

example.q: The Harappan site famous for a bead-making workshop, and the only major city without a citadel, is —
example.solution: **Chanhudaro** (Sindh, Pakistan). Excavated by N.G. Majumdar in 1931.

patterns.name: Site ↔ state/river, and the four extremes
patterns.howToSpot: 'In which state is …?', 'the northernmost/easternmost Harappan site is', or a site-to-river match.
patterns.logic:
1. Split sites first into Pakistan (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Chanhudaro, Kot Diji, Sutkagendor) and India.
2. Indian sites by state: Gujarat (Lothal, Dholavira, Surkotada), Haryana (Rakhigarhi, Banawali), Rajasthan (Kalibangan), Punjab (Ropar), UP (Alamgirpur), Maharashtra (Daimabad), J&K (Manda).
3. Extremes in order N-S-E-W: **Manda, Daimabad, Alamgirpur, Sutkagendor**.

example.q: Which Harappan site lies in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan, on the now-dry Ghaggar river?
example.solution: **Kalibangan** ('black bangles') — known for its ploughed field and fire altars.

patterns.name: Discovery ↔ excavator and year
patterns.howToSpot: 'Who excavated …?', '… was discovered in which year?', 'which site was dug first after Independence?'
patterns.logic:
1. Anchor dates: Harappa 1921 (Daya Ram Sahni), Mohenjo-daro 1922 (R.D. Banerji), announcement 1924 (John Marshall).
2. Later digs: Lothal 1954-55 (S.R. Rao), Ropar 1953 (Y.D. Sharma — first after Independence), Kalibangan 1960s (B.B. Lal & B.K. Thapar), Dholavira 1990 (R.S. Bisht).
3. Match the excavator to the site, not to the civilisation as a whole.

example.q: Mohenjo-daro was excavated in 1922 by —
example.solution: **R.D. Banerji**. Harappa (1921) was dug by **Daya Ram Sahni**; both worked under John Marshall.

patterns.name: Town planning, materials and economy facts
patterns.howToSpot: Statement questions on burnt bricks, grid plans, drainage, seals, crops, metals or weights.
patterns.logic:
1. Planning: grid streets, covered drains, citadel (west) + lower town (east), burnt bricks in ratio 1:2:4.
2. Economy: wheat-barley staple, cotton first grown here, steatite seals, unicorn bull commonest, trade with Mesopotamia.
3. Metals: copper, bronze, gold, silver — **never iron**. Horse evidence is doubtful (only Surkotada bones).

example.q:
Consider the statements about Harappan town planning:
1. Streets cut one another at right angles in a grid pattern.
2. Houses were built mainly of sun-dried bricks.
3. The citadel lay to the west and the lower town to the east.
Which are correct?
example.solution: **1 and 3 only.** The Harappans used **burnt** bricks (ratio 1:2:4), not sun-dried ones — statement 2 is wrong.

patterns.name: Religion, script and society statements
patterns.howToSpot: Questions on Mother Goddess, Pashupati seal, undeciphered script, burial customs, or 'which deity is NOT attested'.
patterns.logic:
1. No temples have been found; worship of Mother Goddess, a proto-Shiva (Pashupati) seal figure, pipal tree.
2. Script: pictographic, right to left, **undeciphered**.
3. In 'NOT attested' questions, look for a well-known Vedic/Puranic deity (Indra, Vishnu) — that is the answer.

example.q:
Which religious element has NOT been found in Harappan sites?
(a) Mother Goddess figurines (b) A proto-Shiva seal (c) Temple structures (d) Pipal-tree motifs
example.solution: (c) **Temple structures** — no temple building has been found at any Harappan site.

subtopics.title: Vedic Age & Vedic Literature
subtopics.concept:
**Timeline:** Early (Rigvedic) Vedic c. 1500–1000 BCE (Sapta Sindhu region, pastoral, cattle = wealth) → Later Vedic c. 1000–600 BCE (Ganga–Yamuna doab, agriculture, iron called *shyama/krishna ayas*, Painted Grey Ware).

**The four Vedas**

| Veda | Content | Priest | Upaveda |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rigveda** | Oldest; **10 mandalas, 1028 hymns** (suktas) of praise | Hotri | Ayurveda |
| **Samaveda** | Rigvedic hymns set to melody — **root of Indian music** | Udgatri | Gandharvaveda |
| **Yajurveda** | Sacrificial formulas; prose + verse; Shukla (white) & Krishna (black) | Adhvaryu | Dhanurveda |
| **Atharvaveda** | Charms, spells, folk medicine; calls **Sabha & Samiti "two daughters of Prajapati"** | Brahma | Shilpaveda |

**Rigveda highlights**
- **Mandala III** – **Gayatri Mantra** (to Savitri), composed by **Vishwamitra**.
- **Mandala VII** – **Battle of Ten Kings** (Dasarajna) on the **Parushni (Ravi)**; **Sudas** of the Bharata clan won.
- **Mandala IX** – wholly addressed to **Soma**.
- **Mandala X** – **Purusha Sukta** (first mention of the four varnas); Nasadiya Sukta (creation hymn).
- Most hymns: **Indra** (~250, called *Purandara*, breaker of forts), then **Agni** (~200); **Varuna** guards *rita* (cosmic order).

**Rivers — Rigvedic vs modern names**

| Rigvedic | Modern | Rigvedic | Modern |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vitasta | Jhelum | Sutudri | Sutlej |
| Asikni | Chenab | Kubha | Kabul |
| Parushni | Ravi | Krumu | Kurram |
| Vipas | Beas | Gomal | Gomati (Gomal) |
| Sindhu | Indus (most mentioned) | Saraswati | "Naditama" – holiest river |
| Drishadvati | Ghaggar/Chautang | Suvastu | Swat |

**Polity & society terms**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Sabha | Council of elders (women attended in early period) |
| Samiti | Popular assembly of the people |
| Vidatha | Oldest tribal assembly |
| Rajan / Purohita / Senani | Chief / priest / army chief |
| Gramani | Village headman |
| Bali | Voluntary tribute → later a tax |
| Bhagadugha | Collector of taxes (later Vedic) |
| Gotra | Lineage; later Vedic rule of gotra exogamy |

**Later Vedic sacrifices:** Rajasuya (consecration), Ashvamedha (horse sacrifice for supremacy), Vajapeya (chariot race). **Four ashramas** (Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha, Sanyasa) — all four first listed in the **Jabala Upanishad**.

**Vedic literature layers:** Samhitas → Brahmanas (ritual prose; e.g. Aitareya, Shatapatha) → Aranyakas (forest texts) → **Upanishads** (philosophy; ~108; *Vedanta*).

| Upanishad | Why asked |
|---|---|
| **Mundaka** | Source of **"Satyameva Jayate"** (national motto) |
| **Katha** | Dialogue of **Nachiketa and Yama** (death) |
| **Brihadaranyaka** | Oldest & largest; Yajnavalkya–Gargi/Maitreyi dialogues |
| **Chandogya** | Early mention of Krishna, son of Devaki |

**Six Vedangas:** Shiksha (phonetics), Kalpa (ritual), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Chhanda (metre), Jyotisha (astronomy).

**Six schools of philosophy (Shad-darshana)**

| School | Founder |
|---|---|
| Sankhya | Kapila |
| Yoga | Patanjali |
| Nyaya | Gautama (Akshapada) |
| Vaisheshika (atomism) | Kanada |
| Purva Mimamsa | Jaimini |
| Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta) | Badarayana |

tricks.title: Punjab rivers west→east: "Very Angry Parrots Visit Sutlej"
tricks.body: **V**itasta = Jhelum → **A**sikni = Chenab → **P**arushni = Ravi → **V**ipas = Beas → **S**utudri = Sutlej. Same order as the modern **J-C-R-B-S**.

example.q: The Rigvedic river Asikni is today's —
example.solution: Second in the chain (V-**A**-P-V-S ↔ J-**C**-R-B-S) → **Chenab**.

tricks.title: Veda → priest: "Rig-Hotri, Sama-Udgatri, Yajur-Adhvaryu, Atharva-Brahma"
tricks.body: Think **HUAB**: **H**otri recites, **U**dgatri sings, **A**dhvaryu performs, **B**rahma supervises.

tricks.title: Rigveda mandala anchors: 3-7-9-10
tricks.body: **3** = Gayatri, **7** = Ten Kings war, **9** = Soma, **10** = Purusha Sukta (varnas).

mistakes: Gayatri Mantra is addressed to **Savitri** (sun deity), not to Gayatri as a goddess; it is in Mandala **III**.
'Satyameva Jayate' is from the **Mundaka** Upanishad, not from the Rigveda.
Most mentioned river = **Sindhu**; most sacred = **Saraswati**. Different answers.
Iron appears only in the **Later** Vedic period.
subtopics.notes:
### Two halves of one age
The Vedic age (c. 1500–600 BCE) is named after the **Vedas**, our main source. It has two phases.
- **Early (Rigvedic) Vedic, c. 1500–1000 BCE:** people lived in the **Sapta Sindhu** (land of seven rivers — Punjab and beyond). Life was **pastoral**; cattle were the main wealth, and the word for war (*gavishthi*, 'search for cows') shows it. Pottery: ochre-coloured and then plain grey.
- **Later Vedic, c. 1000–600 BCE:** people moved into the **Ganga–Yamuna doab**. **Iron** (*shyama ayas* / *krishna ayas*, 'dark metal') appears and agriculture expands. Pottery: **Painted Grey Ware (PGW)**. Kingdoms replace tribes, and the varna system hardens.

### The four Vedas
| Veda | Content | Reciting priest |
|---|---|---|
| Rigveda | Oldest; 10 mandalas, 1028 hymns | Hotri |
| Samaveda | Rigvedic hymns set to melody — root of Indian music | Udgatri |
| Yajurveda | Sacrificial formulas (prose + verse) | Adhvaryu |
| Atharvaveda | Charms, spells, folk medicine | Brahma |

The Rigveda is the oldest text of the Indo-European world still in use as scripture. Each Veda has attached texts: the **Brahmanas** (ritual prose — Aitareya with the Rigveda, Shatapatha with the Yajurveda), then **Aranyakas** (forest teachings) and finally the **Upanishads** (philosophy, also called *Vedanta*). The six limbs of the Vedas (**Vedangas**) are Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda and Jyotisha.

### Rigveda anchors
Exams love four mandalas: **III, VII, IX, X**.
- **Mandala III** — the **Gayatri Mantra**, addressed to **Savitri**, composed by **Vishwamitra**.
- **Mandala VII** — the **Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna)** on the river **Parushni (Ravi)**; **Sudas**, chief of the Bharatas, won.
- **Mandala IX** — entirely devoted to **Soma**.
- **Mandala X** — the **Purusha Sukta**, which first mentions the four varnas (Brahmin from the mouth, Kshatriya from arms, Vaishya from thighs, Shudra from feet).

**Indra** is praised in the most hymns (about 250; *Purandara*, 'fort-breaker'), then **Agni** (about 200), the messenger god; **Varuna** upholds *rita*, the cosmic order. The **Sindhu** is the most-mentioned river, but the **Saraswati** is called the holiest (*naditama*).

### Rivers: Rigvedic names ↔ modern names
| Rigvedic | Modern | Rigvedic | Modern |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vitasta | Jhelum | Vipas | Beas |
| Asikni | Chenab | Sutudri | Sutlej |
| Parushni | Ravi | Kubha | Kabul |
| Drishadvati | Ghaggar–Chautang | Krumu | Kurram |

### Early vs Later Vedic society and polity
| Point | Early Vedic | Later Vedic |
|---|---|---|
| Region | Sapta Sindhu | Ganga–Yamuna doab |
| Economy | Pastoral, cattle wealth | Agriculture, iron |
| Women's status | Comparatively better (Sabha open to women; poetesses like Lopamudra, Apala) | Declines; child marriage appears |
| Assemblies | Sabha, Samiti, Vidatha (all active) | Sabha & Samiti lose power to the king |
| Officers | Rajan, Purohita, Senani, Gramani | Add Bhagadugha (tax collector), Sangrahitri (treasurer) |
| Tax | **Bali** — voluntary tribute | Bali becomes a regular tax |
| Varna | Flexible | Rigid; gotra exogamy rule |

Later Vedic kings performed grand sacrifices to show power: **Rajasuya** (consecration), **Ashvamedha** (horse released to claim supremacy), **Vajapeya** (chariot race). The **four ashramas** (Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha, Sanyasa) are all first listed together in the **Jabala Upanishad**.

### Upanishads and the six schools (Shad-darshana)
| Upanishad | Remember for |
|---|---|
| Mundaka | Source of the national motto **'Satyameva Jayate'** |
| Katha | Dialogue of **Nachiketa** with **Yama** |
| Brihadaranyaka | Oldest and largest; **Yajnavalkya–Gargi** debate |
| Chandogya | Early mention of **Krishna, son of Devaki** |

The six orthodox schools with founders: **Sankhya–Kapila, Yoga–Patanjali, Nyaya–Gautama (Akshapada), Vaisheshika–Kanada, Purva Mimamsa–Jaimini, Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta)–Badarayana**.

### Quick revision
- Early Vedic = pastoral, Sapta Sindhu, flexible society; Later Vedic = iron + agriculture, doab, PGW, rigid varna.
- Veda-priest pairs: Rig-Hotri, Sama-Udgatri, Yajur-Adhvaryu, Atharva-Brahma.
- Mandalas: 3 Gayatri, 7 Ten Kings, 9 Soma, 10 Purusha Sukta.
- Rivers: Vitasta-Jhelum, Asikni-Chenab, Parushni-Ravi, Vipas-Beas, Sutudri-Sutlej.
- 'Satyameva Jayate' — Mundaka Upanishad. Oldest Upanishad — Brihadaranyaka.
- Darshana founders: Kapila, Patanjali, Gautama, Kanada, Jaimini, Badarayana.

patterns.name: Veda ↔ priest / upaveda / content
patterns.howToSpot: 'Which Veda is called…', 'the priest who recites the Samaveda', 'Dhanurveda is attached to which Veda'.
patterns.logic:
1. Recall the four Vedas with their priests: Rig-Hotri, Sama-Udgatri, Yajur-Adhvaryu, Atharva-Brahma.
2. Upavedas: Ayurveda-Rig, Gandharvaveda-Sama, Dhanurveda-Yajur, Shilpaveda-Atharva.
3. Trap: the Atharvaveda is the 'Veda of magical formulas', and is the latest addition to the Vedic corpus.

example.q: Which Veda is partly in prose and partly in verse, and contains sacrificial formulas?
example.solution: The **Yajurveda** — its Shukla (white) and Krishna (black) recensions mix verse and prose ritual formulas.

patterns.name: Rigveda mandala ↔ content; deities of hymns
patterns.howToSpot: Gayatri Mantra, Battle of Ten Kings, Soma, Purusha Sukta, 'maximum hymns to which god'.
patterns.logic:
1. Anchor mandalas: **3 = Gayatri (Vishwamitra, to Savitri)**, **7 = Battle of Ten Kings**, **9 = Soma**, **10 = Purusha Sukta (four varnas)**.
2. Hymn counts: Indra most (~250), Agni next (~200), Varuna guards rita.
3. Dasarajna details: river Parushni (Ravi), winner Sudas of the Bharatas.

example.q: The Gayatri Mantra of the Rigveda was composed by —
example.solution: **Rishi Vishwamitra**; it occurs in **Mandala III** and is addressed to **Savitri** (the solar deity).

patterns.name: Rigvedic river ↔ modern name
patterns.howToSpot: A Rigvedic river name (Vitasta, Asikni, Parushni, Vipas, Sutudri) with modern rivers as options, or the reverse.
patterns.logic:
1. Learn the west-to-east chain: Vitasta-Jhelum, Asikni-Chenab, Parushni-Ravi, Vipas-Beas, Sutudri-Sutlej.
2. Order trick: the Rigvedic names run in the same order as the modern J-C-R-B-S.
3. Extras: Kubha = Kabul, Krumu = Kurram, Drishadvati = Ghaggar-Chautang.

example.q: The Rigvedic river **Vitasta** is known today as —
example.solution: The **Jhelum**. Vitasta is still the Kashmiri name of the Jhelum (Vyeth).

patterns.name: Early vs Later Vedic life and polity terms
patterns.howToSpot: Statement comparisons (early vs later Vedic) or single-term questions on Bali, Vidatha, sabha-samiti, iron, PGW.
patterns.logic:
1. Direction of change: pastoral → agricultural; Sapta Sindhu → doab; assemblies weaken → kings strengthen; Bali voluntary → regular tax.
2. Terms: Vidatha = oldest assembly; Bali = tribute; Bhagadugha = tax collector; Gramani = village head.
3. Iron in Later Vedic = shyama/krishna ayas; pottery = Painted Grey Ware.

example.q: In the Rigvedic period, **Bali** was —
example.solution: A **voluntary tribute** offered by the people to the chief; only in Later Vedic times did it become a regular tax.

patterns.name: Upanishad ↔ content; darshana ↔ founder
patterns.howToSpot: 'Satyameva Jayate is taken from', 'the founder of the Nyaya school', 'Nachiketa appears in'.
patterns.logic:
1. Upanishad anchors: Mundaka = 'Satyameva Jayate'; Katha = Nachiketa-Yama; Brihadaranyaka = oldest, Gargi-Yajnavalkya; Chandogya = Krishna Devaki-putra mention.
2. Darshana founders: Sankhya-Kapila, Yoga-Patanjali, Nyaya-Gautama, Vaisheshika-Kanada, Mimamsa-Jaimini, Vedanta-Badarayana.
3. All six schools accept Vedic authority — that is what 'orthodox (astika)' means.

example.q: The philosophical school of **Vaisheshika**, known for its atomic theory, was founded by —
example.solution: **Kanada** (also called Uluka). The Nyaya school of logic was founded by Gautama (Akshapada).

subtopics.title: Mahajanapadas & Rise of Magadha
subtopics.concept:
**16 Mahajanapadas** (6th century BCE) are listed in the Buddhist text **Anguttara Nikaya** (Jain *Bhagavati Sutra* gives a different list).

| Mahajanapada | Capital | Present region |
|---|---|---|
| Anga | **Champa** | Bhagalpur–Munger, Bihar |
| **Magadha** | **Girivraja / Rajagriha**, later **Pataliputra** | Patna–Gaya, Bihar |
| Kashi | **Varanasi** | UP |
| Kosala | **Shravasti** (also Ayodhya/Saket) | Eastern UP |
| Vajji | **Vaishali** | North Bihar — confederacy of 8 clans incl. **Licchavis** (republic) |
| Malla | **Kushinara** & Pava | Gorakhpur area, UP (republic) |
| Chedi | Shuktimati | Bundelkhand |
| Vatsa | **Kaushambi** | Near Prayagraj, UP |
| Kuru | **Indraprastha** | Delhi–Meerut–Haryana |
| Panchala | Ahichchhatra (N) & Kampilya (S) | Rohilkhand, western UP |
| Matsya | **Viratnagar** | Jaipur–Alwar, Rajasthan |
| Surasena | **Mathura** | UP |
| **Assaka (Ashmaka)** | Potana/Potali | On the Godavari — **only one south of the Vindhyas** |
| **Avanti** | **Ujjain** (N) & **Mahishmati** (S) | Malwa, MP |
| Gandhara | **Taxila** | Rawalpindi–Peshawar, Pakistan |
| Kamboja | Rajapura | NW frontier — famous for **horses** |

**Four great powers:** Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti → **Magadha** emerged supreme (iron mines, fertile Ganga plain, elephants, natural forts at Rajagriha).

**Magadhan dynasties**

| Dynasty | Key rulers & facts |
|---|---|
| **Haryanka** | **Bimbisara** (contemporary of Buddha & Mahavira; marriage alliances with Kosala, Licchavi, Madra; annexed Anga) · **Ajatashatru** (killed his father; fought Vajjis; **First Buddhist Council**) · **Udayin** (founded **Pataliputra** at the Ganga–Son confluence) |
| **Shishunaga** | Shishunaga (destroyed **Avanti**) · **Kalashoka/Kakavarna** (**Second Buddhist Council**, Vaishali) |
| **Nanda** | **Mahapadma Nanda** — first non-Kshatriya empire-builder, titles *Ekarat*, *Sarvakshatrantaka* · **Dhana Nanda** — last; contemporary of Alexander; overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya |

**Foreign invasions**
- **Persian (Achaemenid):** Darius I annexed Gandhara/Punjab (c. 516 BCE) — brought **Kharosthi** script (written right to left) and Aramaic influence.
- **Alexander (326 BCE):** crossed the Indus, fought **Porus (Puru)** at the **Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum)**; troops refused to go beyond the **Beas (Hyphasis)**; died at Babylon in 323 BCE.

tricks.title: Capital pairs by first letter
tricks.body: **K**osala–shravasti? No: use **"Vatsa-Kaushambi, Vajji-Vaishali"** (both V) and **"Avanti-Ujjain, Anga-Champa"** (both start with A). **Kuru-Indraprastha**, **Gandhara-Taxila** (G-T like 'GT road' ending in the north-west).

tricks.title: Magadha order: "Hari Shishu Nanda"
tricks.body: **Hary**anka → **Shishu**naga → **Nanda** → Maurya. Councils: Ajatashatru (1st) is Haryanka, Kalashoka (2nd) is Shishunaga.

example.q: The Second Buddhist Council was held under which dynasty?
example.solution: Kalashoka → **Shishunaga** dynasty (Vaishali, 383 BCE).

mistakes: Pataliputra was founded by **Udayin**, not Ajatashatru (Ajatashatru fortified a small fort, Pataligrama).
Assaka is the lone Mahajanapada **south** of the Vindhyas; Avanti is north (Malwa).
Alexander's army mutinied at the **Beas**, not the Jhelum; the Jhelum (Hydaspes) was the battle with Porus.
subtopics.notes:
### From tribes to territories
By the 6th century BCE (the age of the Buddha and Mahavira), north India had moved from tribe-based society to **territorial states**. The Buddhist text **Anguttara Nikaya** lists **16 mahajanapadas** (great kingdoms/republics); the Jain *Bhagavati Sutra* gives a slightly different list. Settled agriculture, iron tools and rising trade made bigger states possible, and a new **punch-marked silver coinage** made taxes and trade easier.

### The sixteen — the ones exams ask
| Mahajanapada | Capital | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Magadha | Girivraja (Rajagriha), later Pataliputra | Became the empire of the age |
| Anga | Champa | Annexed by Bimbisara |
| Kosala | Shravasti (also Ayodhya) | Fought Magadha over Kashi |
| Kashi | Varanasi | Absorbed by Kosala/Magadha |
| Vajji | Vaishali | Republic of 8 clans incl. Licchavis |
| Malla | Kushinara, Pava | Republic; Buddha died here |
| Vatsa | Kaushambi | King Udayana of legend |
| Kuru | Indraprastha | — |
| Panchala | Ahichchhatra, Kampilya | — |
| Matsya | Viratnagar | Jaipur-Alwar region |
| Surasena | Mathura | — |
| Chedi | Shuktimati | Bundelkhand |
| Avanti | Ujjain (N), Mahishmati (S) | Malwa; rival of Magadha |
| Assaka (Ashmaka) | Potana | **Only one south of the Vindhyas** |
| Gandhara | Taxila | North-west |
| Kamboja | Rajapura | Noted for horses |

### Why Magadha won
The four great powers of the day were **Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti**. Magadha beat all of them because it had: (1) **iron ores** (south Bihar) for weapons and ploughs; (2) the fertile, rain-fed **middle Ganga plain**; (3) **elephants** from the forests for the army; (4) cheap river transport; and (5) naturally defended capitals (Rajagriha ringed by five hills, then Pataliputra girt by rivers). Ambitious, unorthodox rulers also helped — Magadha did not care for the old rules of 'righteous' war.

### The Magadhan dynasties in order
| Dynasty | Rulers and events |
|---|---|
| **Haryanka** | **Bimbisara** — contemporary of **both Buddha and Mahavira**; marriage alliances; annexed Anga; capital Rajagriha. **Ajatashatru** — killed his father; defeated the Vajji confederacy (after 16 years of war); **First Buddhist Council** held under him. **Udayin** — founded **Pataliputra** at the Ganga–Son confluence |
| **Shishunaga** | **Shishunaga** — finally destroyed **Avanti** (its old rival). **Kalashoka** — shifted capital to Pataliputra; **Second Buddhist Council** at Vaishali under him |
| **Nanda** | **Mahapadma Nanda** — 'first empire builder', called *Ekarat* (sole sovereign) and *Sarvakshatrantaka* (destroyer of Kshatriyas); a low-born (non-Kshatriya) ruler. **Dhana Nanda** — last Nanda; contemporary of **Alexander**; overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya with Chanakya |

### Foreign intrusions of the same era
- **Persians (Achaemenids):** Darius I (c. 516 BCE) annexed Sind, Gandhara and western Punjab. Persian contact brought the **Kharosthi script** (written right to left) used in some Ashokan edicts.
- **Alexander of Macedon (326 BCE):** crossed the Indus, defeated **Porus (Puru)** at the **Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum)** — but was so impressed by Porus that he restored his kingdom. At the **Beas (Hyphasis)** his war-weary troops **refused to march further** east (fear of the mighty Nanda army). Alexander went back and died at Babylon in 323 BCE. His invasion opened the land route to Europe and Greek accounts of India.

### Quick revision
- Source list of 16 mahajanapadas: **Anguttara Nikaya** (Buddhist).
- Capital pairs to master: Avanti-Ujjain, Vatsa-Kaushambi, Kosala-Shravasti, Anga-Champa, Gandhara-Taxila, Matsya-Viratnagar.
- Assaka = only mahajanapada **south of the Vindhyas**.
- Dynasty chain: **Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya**.
- Bimbisara (contemporary of Buddha and Mahavira) → Ajatashatru (1st Council) → Udayin (founded Pataliputra) → Shishunaga (ended Avanti) → Kalashoka (2nd Council) → Mahapadma Nanda (Ekarat) → Dhana Nanda (last).
- Persians under Darius I brought Kharosthi; Alexander beat Porus at the Jhelum (326 BCE) and stopped at the Beas.

patterns.name: Mahajanapada ↔ capital
patterns.howToSpot: A capital or mahajanapada given with four options, or 'which pair is correctly matched'.
patterns.logic:
1. Master the six traps: Avanti-Ujjain, Vatsa-Kaushambi, Kosala-Shravasti, Anga-Champa, Gandhara-Taxila, Matsya-Viratnagar.
2. Republics had cities, not 'capitals' in the royal sense: Vajji-Vaishali, Malla-Kushinara/Pava.
3. Magadha had two capitals in sequence: Rajagriha (Girivraja), then Pataliputra from Udayin's time.

example.q: The capital of the Vatsa mahajanapada was —
example.solution: **Kaushambi**, near present-day Prayagraj in UP; its famous king was Udayana.

patterns.name: Magadhan dynasty ↔ ruler and event
patterns.howToSpot: 'Who founded Pataliputra?', 'under which dynasty was the Second Council held?', ordering of Haryanka-Shishunaga-Nanda rulers.
patterns.logic:
1. Dynasty chain: **Haryanka (Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Udayin) → Shishunaga (Shishunaga, Kalashoka) → Nanda (Mahapadma, Dhana)**.
2. Anchor events: Bimbisara annexed Anga; Ajatashatru beat the Vajjis + 1st Council; Udayin founded Pataliputra; Shishunaga destroyed Avanti; Kalashoka 2nd Council; Mahapadma Nanda = Ekarat; Dhana Nanda met Alexander.
3. Council hooks: councils 1-2 go with Ajatashatru (Haryanka) and Kalashoka (Shishunaga).

example.q: Who founded **Pataliputra** on the confluence of the Ganga and the Son?
example.solution: **Udayin**, the Haryanka successor of Ajatashatru. The earlier capital was Rajagriha (Girivraha).

patterns.name: Sixteen mahajanapadas — source text and odd facts
patterns.howToSpot: 'The list of 16 mahajanapadas occurs in', 'which mahajanapada was a republic', 'the only one south of the Vindhyas'.
patterns.logic:
1. Source: **Anguttara Nikaya** (Buddhist); Jain list (Bhagavati Sutra) differs.
2. Republics (gana-sanghas): **Vajji** (with Licchavis) and **Malla**; also later Shakya and Licchavi clans.
3. Geography extremes: Assaka south of the Vindhyas; Kamboja farthest north-west, famous for horses.

example.q: The list of sixteen mahajanapadas appears in which Buddhist text?
example.solution: The **Anguttara Nikaya**, part of the Sutta Pitaka. The Jain Bhagavati Sutra gives a different list of sixteen.

patterns.name: Persian and Alexander's invasions
patterns.howToSpot: Questions on Darius I, Kharosthi script, the Hydaspes battle with Porus, the mutiny at the Beas.
patterns.logic:
1. Persians: **Darius I, c. 516 BCE** annexed Gandhara/west Punjab; gift to India = the **Kharosthi script** (right to left).
2. Alexander, **326 BCE**: crossed the Indus; **beat Porus at the Hydaspes (Jhelum)** and restored him.
3. Mutiny at the **Beas (Hyphasis)** — not the Jhelum; died at Babylon **323 BCE**.

example.q: Alexander's army refused to march beyond which river?
example.solution: The **Beas (Hyphasis)** — the soldiers, tired and hearing of the vast Nanda army beyond, mutinied and forced the return march.

subtopics.title: Buddhism & Jainism
subtopics.concept:
**Gautama Buddha (c. 563–483 BCE, traditional dates)**

| Event | Place / fact | Symbol |
|---|---|---|
| Birth | **Lumbini** (Nepal); Shakya clan; father Suddhodana, mother Mahamaya (foster mother Prajapati Gautami) | Lotus & bull |
| Great Renunciation (*Mahabhinishkramana*) | Age 29; horse **Kanthaka**, charioteer **Channa** | Horse |
| Enlightenment (*Nirvana/Sambodhi*) | Age 35, **Bodh Gaya**, under the pipal (Bodhi) tree on the **Niranjana (Falgu)** | Bodhi tree |
| First sermon (*Dharmachakra-pravartana*) | **Sarnath** (Deer Park, Rishipatana) | Wheel |
| Death (*Mahaparinirvana*) | Age 80, **Kushinagar** (Malla republic) | Stupa |

Wife **Yashodhara**, son **Rahula**. Teachings in **Pali**. **Tri-ratna:** Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha. **Four Noble Truths** (suffering, its cause, its end, the path) and **Eightfold Path** (*Ashtangika Marga*) — the "Middle Path".

**Buddhist Councils (Sangiti)**

| Council | Year | Place | King | President | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | 483 BCE | **Rajagriha** (Saptaparni cave) | **Ajatashatru** | **Mahakassapa** | Sutta (by **Ananda**) & Vinaya (by **Upali**) compiled |
| 2nd | 383 BCE | **Vaishali** | **Kalashoka** | **Sabakami** | Split: Sthaviravadins vs Mahasanghikas |
| 3rd | 250 BCE | **Pataliputra** | **Ashoka** | **Moggaliputta Tissa** | **Abhidhamma Pitaka** added; missions abroad |
| 4th | c. 72 CE | **Kundalvana, Kashmir** | **Kanishka** | **Vasumitra** (deputy **Ashvaghosha**) | Split into **Hinayana & Mahayana** |

**Tripitaka:** *Vinaya* (monastic rules), *Sutta* (discourses), *Abhidhamma* (philosophy). **Jatakas** = stories of Buddha's previous births. **Milindapanha** = dialogue of Indo-Greek king **Menander** with monk **Nagasena**. Mahayana philosopher **Nagarjuna** (Madhyamika) — "Einstein of India" (a popular tag). Future Buddha = **Maitreya**; Padmapani = **Avalokiteshvara**.

**Jainism — 24 Tirthankaras**

| No. | Tirthankara | Symbol |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Rishabhanatha (Adinatha)** | Bull |
| 22 | Neminatha (Arishtanemi) | Conch |
| 23 | **Parshvanatha** — prince of Varanasi (son of Ashvasena); gave **4 vows** | Snake |
| 24 | **Vardhamana Mahavira** | Lion |

**Mahavira (traditional 540–468 BCE):** born **Kundagrama** near Vaishali; father **Siddhartha** (Jnatrika clan), mother **Trishala** (Licchavi princess, sister of Chetaka); wife Yashoda, daughter Anojja (Priyadarshana). **Kaivalya** at 42 under a sal tree at **Jrimbhikagrama** on the **Rijupalika**; died at **Pavapuri** (near Rajgir) at 72. Added the **5th vow — Brahmacharya**. Titles: *Jina* (conqueror), *Nirgrantha* (free from bonds).

- **Five vows:** Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha, Brahmacharya.
- **Tri-ratna (Jain):** Right faith, Right knowledge, Right conduct.
- **Sects:** **Digambara** (sky-clad; led by **Bhadrabahu**, migrated south with Chandragupta Maurya) vs **Shvetambara** (white-clad; **Sthulabhadra**).
- **Jain councils:** 1st at **Pataliputra** (c. 300 BCE, president **Sthulabhadra**; 12 Angas compiled) · 2nd at **Vallabhi**, Gujarat (5th–6th century CE, president **Devarddhi Kshamasramana**; canon finally written).
- Language: **Prakrit (Ardhamagadhi)**. *Kalpasutra* attributed to **Bhadrabahu**.
- Monuments: **Gommateshwara (Bahubali)** monolith at **Shravanabelagola** (Karnataka, c. 983 CE, by **Chamundaraya**, minister of the Western Gangas; *Mahamastakabhisheka* every 12 years); **Dilwara temples** (Mount Abu).

**Buddhist learning centres:** Nalanda (founded by Gupta king **Kumaragupta I**), **Vikramashila** (Pala king **Dharmapala**), **Odantapuri** (Pala king Gopala), Taxila.

tricks.title: Councils — places "Raja Vaishali Pata Kashmir", kings alternate "A-K-A-K"
tricks.body: Places: **Raj**agriha → **Vaish**ali → **Pat**aliputra → **Kash**mir. Kings: **A**jatashatru, **K**alashoka, **A**shoka, **K**anishka. Presidents: **"Maha-Saba-Moggali-Vasu"**.

example.q: Who presided over the Third Buddhist Council?
example.solution: Third = Pataliputra / Ashoka → **Moggaliputta Tissa**.

tricks.title: Buddha's life symbols: "Lotus → Horse → Tree → Wheel → Stupa"
tricks.body: Birth, renunciation, enlightenment, first sermon, death — in that order.

tricks.title: Tirthankara symbols: "Bull begins, Lion ends"
tricks.body: 1st Rishabha = bull, 22nd = conch, 23rd Parshva = **s**nake (**S**erpent), 24th Mahavira = lion.

mistakes: Mahavira **added** Brahmacharya; the other four vows came from Parshvanatha.
Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, first sermon at **Sarnath**, death at **Kushinagar** — do not confuse Sarnath with Bodh Gaya.
The 4th Buddhist Council (Kanishka) split the order into Hinayana/Mahayana; the 2nd split it into Sthaviravadin/Mahasanghika.
Nalanda was founded by the **Guptas** (Kumaragupta I); Vikramashila by the **Palas**.
subtopics.notes:
### Two protest faiths of the 6th century BCE
Buddhism and Jainism began in the same age, in the same belt (Magadha-Vaishali), and for similar reasons: rising taxes and animal sacrifice in ritual religion, Sanskrit scriptures closed to ordinary people, and a new trading class (sethis) looking for simpler, ethical faiths. Both rejected Vedic ritual's authority, preached **ahimsa** and used the people's language (**Pali** for early Buddhism, **Prakrit/Ardhamagadhi** for Jainism). Both were supported by kings and merchants alike.

### The life of the Buddha — five stations
| Event | Place | Symbol |
|---|---|---|
| Birth (563 BCE, traditional) | **Lumbini** (Nepal) | Lotus & bull |
| Renunciation (Mahabhinishkramana, age 29) | Left Kapilavastu on horse Kanthaka with charioteer Channa | Horse |
| Enlightenment (age 35) | **Bodh Gaya**, under the Bodhi tree by the Niranjana (Falgu) | Bodhi tree |
| First sermon (Dharmachakra-pravartana) | **Sarnath** (Deer Park) | Wheel |
| Death (Mahaparinirvana, age 80) | **Kushinagar** (Malla republic) | Stupa |

Born a **Shakya** prince (father Suddhodana, mother Mahamaya), he married Yashodhara (son Rahul). The teaching: **Four Noble Truths** (the world is sorrow; desire causes sorrow; sorrow can end; the Eightfold Path ends it) and the **Eightfold Path** — the **Middle Path** between luxury and severe austerity. **Tri-ratna** of Buddhism: Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha. Teachings were compiled in **Pali** into the **Tripitaka** — *Vinaya Pitaka* (monastic rules), *Sutta Pitaka* (discourses), *Abhidhamma Pitaka* (philosophy). The **Jatakas** are stories of the Buddha's former births.

### The four Buddhist Councils
| Council | Place | King | President | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st (483 BCE) | Rajagriha (Saptaparni cave) | Ajatashatru | Mahakassapa | Sutta (Ananda) & Vinaya (Upali) compiled |
| 2nd (383 BCE) | Vaishali | Kalashoka | Sabakami | Split: Sthaviravadins vs Mahasanghikas |
| 3rd (250 BCE) | Pataliputra | Ashoka | Moggaliputta Tissa | Abhidhamma Pitaka added; missions sent |
| 4th (c. 72 CE) | Kundalvana, Kashmir | Kanishka | Vasumitra (deputy Ashvaghosha) | Split into Hinayana & Mahayana |

Learn the chains: places **Raj-Vaish-Pat-Kash**, kings **A-K-A-K**, presidents **Maha-Saba-Moggali-Vasu**.

### Jainism — the 24 Tirthankaras
Jainism claims **24 Tirthankaras** (ford-makers). The exam set: **1st Rishabhanatha (Adinatha, symbol bull)**; 22nd Neminatha (conch); **23rd Parshvanatha** (prince of Varanasi, son of Ashvasena; symbol snake; gave **four vows** — ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha); **24th Vardhamana Mahavira** (symbol lion).

**Mahavira** (traditional 540–468 BCE) was born at **Kundagrama** near Vaishali (father Siddhartha of the Jnatrika clan; mother Trishala, sister of the Licchavi chief Chetaka). He attained **kaivalya** (omniscience) at 42 under a sal tree at Jrimbhikagrama and died at **Pavapuri** at 72. He **added the fifth vow, Brahmacharya**. His titles: *Jina* (conqueror — hence 'Jain'), *Nirgrantha* (free of bonds). The **Tri-ratna of Jainism** is Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct.

**Sects:** after the great famine, **Digambaras** (sky-clad; leader **Bhadrabahu**, who went south with Chandragupta Maurya) vs **Shvetambaras** (white-clad; **Sthulabhadra**). **Councils:** 1st at **Pataliputra** (c. 300 BCE, Sthulabhadra; 12 Angas compiled), 2nd at **Vallabhi** (Gujarat, 5th–6th century CE, **Devarddhi**; canon written down). The *Kalpasutra* is attributed to Bhadrabahu.

### Texts, sects and monuments
- **Milindapanha** — dialogue of Indo-Greek king **Menander (Milinda)** with the monk **Nagasena**.
- **Mahayana** philosopher **Nagarjuna** (Madhyamika school); future Buddha **Maitreya**; Padmapani = Avalokiteshvara.
- Monuments: **Gommateshwara (Bahubali)** statue, **Shravanabelagola** (Karnataka, c. 983 CE, built by Chamundaraya, minister of the Western Ganga kings; Mahamastakabhisheka every 12 years); **Dilwara** Jain temples, Mount Abu.
- Monasteries: **Nalanda** (founded by Gupta king **Kumaragupta I**), **Vikramashila** (Pala king **Dharmapala**), **Odantapuri** (Pala king Gopala).

### Quick revision
- Life chain: Lumbini → (renunciation) → Bodh Gaya → Sarnath → Kushinagar; symbols lotus-horse-tree-wheel-stupa.
- Councils: Rajagriha, Vaishali, Pataliputra, Kashmir; kings A-K-A-K; presidents Maha-Saba-Moggali-Vasu.
- 4th Council (Kanishka) = Hinayana/Mahayana split; 2nd = Sthaviravada/Mahasanghika split.
- Tirthankaras: 1 bull, 22 conch, 23 snake (Parshva, 4 vows), 24 lion (Mahavira, added 5th vow).
- Jain sects Digambara/Shvetambara; councils Pataliputra & Vallabhi; Gommateshwara at Shravanabelagola.
- Nalanda = Kumaragupta I (Gupta); Vikramashila = Dharmapala (Pala).

patterns.name: Buddha's life events ↔ places and symbols
patterns.howToSpot: 'Where did the Buddha attain enlightenment?', 'the symbol of Mahaparinirvana', ordering of life events.
patterns.logic:
1. Life chain: Lumbini (birth) → renunciation (age 29) → Bodh Gaya (enlightenment, 35) → Sarnath (first sermon) → Kushinagar (death, 80).
2. Symbols in order: lotus-bull, horse, Bodhi tree, wheel, stupa.
3. River and helpers: Niranjana (Falgu) at Bodh Gaya; horse Kanthaka, charioteer Channa; wife Yashodhara, son Rahul.

example.q: Where did Gautama Buddha attain **Mahaparinirvana**?
example.solution: At **Kushinagar** (Kasia, UP), in the territory of the Malla republic, at the age of 80.

patterns.name: Buddhist councils ↔ place, king, president, outcome
patterns.howToSpot: 'The Fourth Council was held under…', 'which council added the Abhidhamma Pitaka', matching council-president pairs.
patterns.logic:
1. Places: Rajagriha → Vaishali → Pataliputra → Kashmir (Kundalvana).
2. Kings: Ajatashatru → Kalashoka → Ashoka → Kanishka (A-K-A-K).
3. Presidents: Mahakassapa → Sabakami → Moggaliputta Tissa → Vasumitra (Maha-Saba-Moggali-Vasu).
4. Outcomes: 2nd = first split (Sthaviravada/Mahasanghika); 3rd = Abhidhamma added; 4th = Hinayana/Mahayana split.

example.q: Which Buddhist council resulted in the split into **Hinayana and Mahayana**?
example.solution: The **Fourth Council** (c. 72 CE, Kundalvana, Kashmir) under **Kanishka**, with **Vasumitra** as president and **Ashvaghosha** as deputy.

patterns.name: Jainism: Tirthankaras, Mahavira's life and vows
patterns.howToSpot: 'Who was the 23rd Tirthankara', 'which vow was added by Mahavira', 'Mahavira attained kaivalya at'.
patterns.logic:
1. Number set: 1 Rishabha (bull), 22 Neminatha (conch), 23 Parshvanatha (snake, four vows), 24 Mahavira (lion).
2. Mahavira's chain: Kundagrama birth → kaivalya at 42 (Jrimbhikagrama, Rijupalika river) → death at Pavapuri at 72.
3. Vows: Parshva gave four (ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha); Mahavira **added Brahmacharya** (celibacy) as the fifth.

example.q: Which vow of Jainism was **added by Mahavira** to the four preached by Parshvanatha?
example.solution: **Brahmacharya** (celibacy). The four older vows were ahimsa, satya, asteya and aparigraha.

patterns.name: Buddhist/Jain texts, sects and monuments
patterns.howToSpot: 'Milindapanha is a dialogue between', 'Gommateshwara statue is at', 'Vikramashila was founded by', Digambara vs Shvetambara.
patterns.logic:
1. Texts: Tripitaka (Vinaya, Sutta, Abhidhamma), Jatakas (previous births), Milindapanha (Menander-Nagasena), Buddhacharita (Ashvaghosha).
2. Jain monuments: Gommateshwara at Shravanabelagola (Chamundaraya, c. 983 CE); Dilwara temples, Mount Abu.
3. Monasteries: Nalanda = Kumaragupta I (Gupta); Vikramashila = Dharmapala (Pala); Odantapuri = Gopala (Pala).

example.q: The *Milindapanha* records a dialogue between the monk Nagasena and which king?
example.solution: The Indo-Greek king **Menander (Milinda)**, who ruled from Sakala (Sialkot).

subtopics.title: Mauryan Empire
subtopics.concept:
**Rulers**

| Ruler | Reign (approx.) | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| **Chandragupta Maurya** | 322–298 BCE | Overthrew Dhana Nanda with **Chanakya (Kautilya/Vishnugupta)**; defeated **Seleucus Nicator** (305 BCE) and got Arachosia, Gedrosia, Paropamisadae, Aria + marriage alliance; Greek name **Sandrocottus**; became a Jain, went to **Shravanabelagola** with **Bhadrabahu** and died by *sallekhana* |
| **Bindusara** | 298–273 BCE | Title **Amitraghata** ("slayer of foes"); Greek envoy **Deimachus** (of Antiochus I); followed the **Ajivika** sect |
| **Ashoka** | c. 268–232 BCE | **Kalinga war 261 BCE** (8th regnal year); turned to Buddhism (monk **Upagupta**); *Dhamma* policy; **Third Buddhist Council** |
| Brihadratha | — | **Last** Mauryan; killed by his general **Pushyamitra Shunga** (c. 185 BCE) |

**Foreign accounts**
- **Megasthenes** — ambassador of **Seleucus Nicator** at Chandragupta's court; wrote **Indica** (lost; survives in later Greek quotes). Described Pataliputra run by **6 committees of 5 members each** and Indian society in **7 "castes"**.
- **Arthashastra** by **Kautilya** — treatise on statecraft, 15 books (*adhikaranas*); rediscovered and published by **R. Shamasastry** (early 1900s).

**Ashoka's inscriptions**

| Type | Facts |
|---|---|
| **14 Major Rock Edicts** | **RE II** – medical care for humans & animals · **RE V** – appointment of **Dhamma Mahamattas** · **RE XII** – tolerance among sects · **RE XIII** – **Kalinga war**, remorse, *dhamma-vijaya* |
| **Separate Kalinga Edicts** | At **Dhauli & Jaugada** (Odisha): "All men are my children" |
| **Minor Rock Edicts** | **Maski** (Raichur, Karnataka) — first found edict that names the king as **"Ashoka"** (also Gujarra, Nittur, Udegolam) |
| **7 Pillar Edicts** | Delhi-Topra pillar has all seven; Topra & Meerut pillars were moved to Delhi by **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** |
| Scripts | Mostly **Brahmi**; **Kharosthi** at Shahbazgarhi & Mansehra (NW); **Greek & Aramaic** at Kandahar (Afghanistan) |
| Decipherment | Brahmi deciphered by **James Prinsep** (1837) |

Ashoka calls himself **"Devanampiya Piyadasi"** (beloved of the gods). **Sarnath Lion Capital** (four lions, chakra, bull–horse–elephant–lion on the abacus) → **National Emblem, adopted 26 January 1950**. Rampurva has a **bull capital**; Lauriya-Nandangarh a single lion. **Allahabad pillar** also carries Samudragupta's *Prayag Prashasti*.

**Administration & economy:** *Samaharta* – chief revenue collector; *Sannidhata* – treasurer; *Sita* – revenue from crown land; land tax usually **1/6** (*bhaga*); spies (*gudhapurushas*); provinces under princes (*kumaras*) at Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali, Suvarnagiri.

**Mauryan art:** highly **polished Chunar sandstone** pillars; **Barabar caves** (Bihar) cut for **Ajivikas** (Lomas Rishi cave); **Didarganj Yakshi** (chauri-bearer, Patna Museum).

tricks.title: Edict numbers: "2-Hospital, 5-Officer, 12-Tolerance, 13-Kalinga"
tricks.body: Think of a hospital ward **2**, officer rank **5**, the **12** faiths tolerated, and the unlucky **13** (war).

example.q: Which Major Rock Edict records Ashoka's remorse after Kalinga?
example.solution: Unlucky **13** → **Rock Edict XIII**.

tricks.title: Mauryan dates chain: 322 → 185 → 73 BCE
tricks.body: Maurya starts **322**, Shunga starts **185** (Pushyamitra), Kanva starts **73** (Vasudeva Kanva).

mistakes: Megasthenes served **Seleucus**; Deimachus served **Antiochus I** (at Bindusara's court).
Chandragupta Maurya was a **Jain** at the end; Bindusara favoured **Ajivikas**; Ashoka became Buddhist.
The name 'Ashoka' appears in **Maski**, not in the Major Rock Edicts, which use 'Devanampiya Piyadasi'.
Brahmi was deciphered by **James Prinsep**, not by John Marshall.
subtopics.notes:
### The first all-India empire
In **322 BCE** **Chandragupta Maurya**, guided by his guru **Kautilya (Chanakya)** — author of the *Arthashastra* on statecraft — overthrew **Dhana Nanda** and founded the Mauryan empire with its capital at **Pataliputra**. At his court lived the Greek ambassador **Megasthenes**, whose book *Indica* (surviving in fragments) describes Pataliputra, the army and the absence of slavery in the Greek sense. In **305 BCE** Chandragupta faced **Seleucus Nicator**, Alexander's general; the treaty gave Seleucus **500 war elephants** while Chandragupta received the eastern satrapies (Kabul–Kandahar–Herat–Makran belt) and a marriage alliance. **Bindusara** ('slayer of foes', *Amitraghata*) kept the Greek envoy **Deimachus** at court. **Ashoka** (c. 268–232 BCE) fought the **Kalinga war in 261 BCE** (his 8th regnal year); the horror of it turned him to **Dhamma** — not a new religion, but a code of ethics: tolerance, ahimsa, kindness to servants and animals, respect for all sects, welfare works (roads, wells, rest houses).

### The edicts
Ashoka's messages are carved on rocks and polished pillars in **Prakrit**, mostly in the **Brahmi script** (Kharosthi in the north-west; a Greek–Aramaic bilingual at Kandahar). They were deciphered by **James Prinsep in 1837**. Key items:
- **Major Rock Edict XIII** — the Kalinga war and the king's remorse; names five Greek kings as neighbours in Dhamma.
- **Major Rock Edict XII** — tolerance and respect for all sects.
- **Bhabru (Bairat) edict** — the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha.
- **Rummindei pillar** — visit to Lumbini (the Buddha's birthplace); village tax reduced to one-eighth.
- **Schism edicts** — unity of the Sangha.
- **Dhamma Mahamatras** — special officers appointed (RE V) to spread Dhamma.

### Administration — a machine state
The king stood at the top, advised by the **mantriparishad** (council of ministers). Provinces (Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali, Suvarnagiri, Pataliputra) were headed by princes (**Kumara**/**Aryaputra**). Revenue officers: **Samaharta** (collection), **Sannidhata** (treasurer–storekeeper), yuktas as accountants; district level **Pradeshika**, **Rajuka** (survey) and **Sthanika**; the village head was the **gramika**. A spy network of **gudhapurusha** ran in two wings — *sanstha* (stationary) and *sanchara* (wandering). Megasthenes counted an army of about 6 lakh infantry, 30,000 cavalry and 9,000 elephants. The state monopolised **mines, salt and liquor** and ran irrigation and roads.

### Mauryan art and architecture
Court art is monolithic and polished: **pillars of Chunar sandstone** with animal capitals — the **Sarnath Lion Capital** (four lions back to back, wheel on the abacus) became India's **National Emblem** on 26 January 1950. Stupa cores at **Sanchi** and the Dharmarajika date to Ashoka; the **Barabar (and Nagarjuni) hill caves** were gifted to the **Ajivika** sect — India's earliest rock-cut caves (Lomas Rishi's chaitya-arch facade). Folk art produced the **Yaksha–Yakshini** statues (e.g. the Didarganj Yakshini with a fly-whisk).

### Decline
Later rulers (Dasharatha onwards) were weak. The empire broke under money trouble, over-centralisation, Greek pressure on the north-west and religious reaction. The last Mauryan king, **Brihadratha**, was killed by his commander **Pushyamitra Sunga in 185 BCE**, who founded the Sunga dynasty.

### Quick revision
- 322 BCE Chandragupta + Chanakya end the Nandas; Megasthenes (*Indica*) at court; Deimachus under Bindusara.
- Seleucus treaty 305 BCE: 500 elephants for eastern satrapies + marriage alliance.
- Kalinga 261 BCE → Dhamma; edicts in Prakrit/Brahmi; deciphered by Prinsep (1837).
- RE XIII = Kalinga remorse; RE XII = tolerance; Bhabru = Buddha-Dhamma-Sangha; Rummindei = Lumbini tax cut.
- Officers: Samaharta (collection), Sannidhata (treasury), Rajuka (survey), gudhapurusha spies (sanstha/sanchara).
- Sarnath Lion Capital = National Emblem; Barabar caves = Ajivikas; 185 BCE Brihadratha → Pushyamitra Sunga.

patterns.name: Ashoka's edicts: which edict carries which message
patterns.howToSpot: 'Which edict describes the Kalinga war', 'where does Ashoka's personal name appear', 'what does the Bhabru edict say', script/language of inscriptions.
patterns.logic:
1. Anchor edicts: **RE XIII = Kalinga remorse**, **RE XII = tolerance**, **Bhabru = Buddha-Dhamma-Sangha**, **Rummindei = Lumbini + tax remission**.
2. Ashoka's personal name appears only in **Maski, Gujarra, Nettur, Udegolam** (Minor Rock Edicts); elsewhere 'Devanampiya Piyadasi'.
3. Language/script: Prakrit + Brahmi mostly; Kharosthi in the north-west; Greek-Aramaic at Kandahar; deciphered by James Prinsep (1837).

example.q: Which Ashokan edict records the king's faith in the **Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha**?
example.solution: The **Bhabru (Bairat) edict** — a Minor Rock Edict found near Jaipur, Rajasthan.

patterns.name: Mauryan administration: officers and machinery
patterns.howToSpot: 'Who was Samaharta/Sannidhata', spy wings sanstha-sanchara, provincial governors, Dhamma Mahamatras.
patterns.logic:
1. Revenue pair: **Samaharta = collector**, **Sannidhata = treasurer/storekeeper**.
2. Field officers: Pradeshika (district), Rajuka (survey/revenue), Sthanika, Gramika (village).
3. Spies: gudhapurusha — sanstha (stationary) and sanchara (wandering); provinces under Kumara princes.

example.q: In Mauryan administration, the officer responsible for the **collection of revenue** was the —
example.solution: **Samaharta**; the **Sannidhata** kept the treasury and storehouses.

patterns.name: Chandragupta, Chanakya and the Greeks
patterns.howToSpot: Founding of the empire, the Arthashastra, the Seleucus treaty terms, Megasthenes' Indica.
patterns.logic:
1. 322 BCE: Chandragupta + Kautilya end Dhana Nanda's rule.
2. Seleucus treaty (305 BCE): **500 elephants ↔ eastern satrapies + marriage alliance**.
3. Visitors: Megasthenes (Chandragupta, *Indica*), Deimachus (Bindusara), Ptolemy's ambassador Dionysius (Ashoka).

example.q: Under the Maurya–Seleucus treaty (305 BCE), Chandragupta handed over to Seleucus —
example.solution: **500 war elephants**; in return he received the eastern satrapies (Kabul–Kandahar–Herat–Makran) and a marriage alliance.

patterns.name: Mauryan art, architecture and the dynasty's end
patterns.howToSpot: Lion Capital and National Emblem, Barabar caves, polished pillars, stupa cores, Brihadratha–Pushyamitra Sunga.
patterns.logic:
1. Court art: polished Chunar-sandstone pillars; **Sarnath Lion Capital = National Emblem** (26 Jan 1950).
2. **Barabar caves = Ajivika sect** — earliest rock-cut caves; Sanchi stupa core is Mauryan.
3. End: **Brihadratha killed by Pushyamitra Sunga, 185 BCE** → Sunga dynasty.

example.q: The Barabar hill caves, excavated in the Mauryan period, were dedicated to which sect?
example.solution: The **Ajivika** sect — they are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves of India, with the Lomas Rishi chaitya-arch facade.

subtopics.title: Post-Mauryan Age: Shungas to Kushanas
subtopics.concept:
**Indigenous dynasties**

| Dynasty | Founder / key rulers | Facts |
|---|---|---|
| **Shunga** (c. 185–73 BCE) | **Pushyamitra Shunga** | Killed Brihadratha; performed **2 Ashvamedhas**; patron of grammarian **Patanjali**; **Agnimitra** is the hero of Kalidasa's *Malavikagnimitram*; **Bharhut** stupa railings |
| **Kanva** (c. 73–28 BCE) | **Vasudeva Kanva** | Killed last Shunga king Devabhuti; ended by the Satavahanas |
| **Satavahana** (Andhras) | Founder **Simuka**; capital **Pratishthana (Paithan)** on the Godavari | **Gautamiputra Satakarni** — greatest; destroyed the Kshaharata Shakas (**Nahapana**); praised in the **Nasik inscription** of his mother **Gautami Balashri**. **Hala** wrote *Gathasaptashati* (Prakrit). First to give **tax-free land grants to Brahmanas**; kings used **metronymics**; **lead** and potin coins; official language **Prakrit** |
| **Chedi (Kalinga)** | **Kharavela** | **Hathigumpha inscription** (Udayagiri, Odisha); Jain patron |

**Foreign dynasties**

| Group | Key ruler | Facts |
|---|---|---|
| **Indo-Greeks** | **Demetrius**, **Menander (Milinda)** — capital **Sakala (Sialkot)** | First coins that can be definitely attributed to kings; **first gold coins** in India; *Milindapanha*; roots of **Gandhara art** |
| **Shakas (Scythians)** | **Rudradaman I** (Western Kshatrapa, Ujjain) | **Junagadh (Girnar) inscription, c. 150 CE** — first long inscription in chaste **Sanskrit**; repaired the **Sudarshana lake** (built by Chandragupta Maurya's governor **Pushyagupta**) |
| **Parthians (Pahlavas)** | **Gondophernes** | Visit of **St. Thomas** (tradition); Takht-i-Bahi inscription |
| **Kushanas** (Yuezhi) | **Kujula Kadphises** → **Vima Kadphises** (large gold issues, Shiva on coins) → **Kanishka** | See below |

**Kanishka (accession 78 CE)**
- Started the **Shaka era (78 CE)** — basis of India's **National Calendar**.
- Capital **Purushapura (Peshawar)**; second centre **Mathura**.
- Convened the **4th Buddhist Council** (Kundalvana, Kashmir); patron of **Mahayana**.
- Court: **Ashvaghosha** (*Buddhacharita*), **Nagarjuna**, **Vasumitra**, physician **Charaka** (*Charaka Samhita*).
- Title *Devaputra*; **Rabatak inscription** (Afghanistan) gives Kushana genealogy.
- Art: **Gandhara school** (Greco-Roman style, grey schist) & **Mathura school** (red sandstone, indigenous).

**Eras**

| Era | Starts | Founder (tradition) |
|---|---|---|
| **Vikram Samvat** | **57 BCE** | Vikramaditya of Ujjain (after defeating Shakas) |
| **Shaka Samvat** | **78 CE** | **Kanishka** — official national calendar |
| Gupta era | 319–320 CE | Chandragupta I |
| Harsha era | 606 CE | Harshavardhana |

tricks.title: "57 minus, 78 plus"
tricks.body: Vikram Samvat = **57 BCE** (subtract), Shaka = **78 CE** (add). To convert: CE = VS − 57; CE = Shaka + 78.

example.q: Shaka year 1948 corresponds to which CE year?
example.solution: 1948 + 78 = **2026 CE** (Shaka year begins on 22 March in a normal year).

tricks.title: Satavahana = "S-P-G-H"
tricks.body: **S**imuka founder · **P**ratishthana capital · **G**autamiputra greatest · **H**ala poet.

mistakes: Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription is in **Sanskrit**; Ashoka's inscriptions are in Prakrit.
Shaka era was begun by **Kanishka** (a Kushana), not by a Shaka ruler.
Charaka was Kanishka's physician; **Sushruta** is the surgeon (Sushruta Samhita).
subtopics.notes:
### After the Mauryas — a crowd of dynasties
Pushyamitra Sunga (185–73 BCE) ruled from Pataliputra with Vidisha as a second centre; the grammarian **Patanjali** (*Mahabhashya*) adorned his age, and existing stupas (Sanchi, Bharhut railings) were expanded. The **Kanvas** (73–28 BCE) succeeded briefly. Then wave after wave of Central-Asian people entered through the north-west.
- **Indo-Greeks (Bactrian Greeks):** best king **Menander (Milinda)**, whose dialogues with the monk **Nagasena** form the *Milindapanha*; they were the **first to issue coins bearing kings' portraits**.
- **Shakas:** five branches; the western branch of Ujjain produced **Rudradaman I** (c. 130 CE), whose **Junagadh rock inscription** is the **first long inscription in chaste Sanskrit** and records the repair of **Sudarshana lake**.
- **Parthians (Pahlavas):** **Gondophernes** is linked in tradition with St Thomas's arrival.
- **Kushanas:** the greatest of them all.

### The Kushanas
**Kujula Kadphises** united the five Yuezhi clans; **Vima Kadphises** issued India's **first gold coins**; **Kanishka** (from **78 CE**, the **Shaka era** used in India's national calendar) ruled from **Purushpura (Peshawar)** with **Mathura** as a second capital. Kanishka patronised the **Fourth Buddhist Council** (Kashmir) — after which Buddhism split into **Hinayana and Mahayana** — and scholars **Ashvaghosha** (*Buddhacharita*), **Charaka** (*Charaka Samhita*), **Vasumitra** and **Nagarjuna**. Two art schools flowered: **Gandhara** (Greco-Buddhist style, grey schist) and **Mathura** (indigenous, red sandstone). Kushana control of the **Silk Road** fed the economy.

### The Satavahanas of the Deccan
Founded by **Simuka** (c. 1st century BCE), with the capital at **Pratishthana (Paithan on the Godavari)**; their coins say 'Andhra'. The greatest ruler **Gautamiputra Satakarni** — 'destroyer of Kshatriyas', 'lord of the Andhra race' — is known chiefly from the **Nasik inscription of his mother, Gautami Balashri**. The Satavahanas were the **first dynasty to make land grants to Brahmanas** (tax-free), a seed of the feudal age; they issued **lead and potin coins** and used **Prakrit**. Their ports (Kalyan, Sopara) carried the Roman trade; their society shows **nahapana-erased coins** and, in some areas, cross-cousin marriage and mothers named on coins (a non-Sanskritic touch).

### Indo-Roman trade
The *Periplus of the Erythraean Sea* and Sangam poems describe Yavana traders at Indian ports: **Tamralipti** (Ganga delta, east), **Bharuch (Bhrigukachchha)** and Sopara (west), **Muziris** (Kerala) and **Arikamedu** (near Pondicherry — arretine Roman pottery, beads, Roman lamps). Big hoards of **Roman gold coins** show the trade balance ran in India's favour — Pliny complained that Rome drained gold for pepper, pearls and textiles.

### Quick revision
- Order of NW entries: Indo-Greeks → Shakas → Parthians → Kushanas; Sunga → Kanva in the heartland.
- Menander-Nagasena = Milindapanha; Indo-Greeks = first portrait coins; Rudradaman = first chaste-Sanskrit inscription + Sudarshana lake.
- Kushana chain: Kujula → **Vima Kadphises (first gold)** → **Kanishka (78 CE Shaka era; Peshawar + Mathura)**.
- Kanishka's circle: Ashvaghosha, Charaka, Vasumitra, Nagarjuna; Gandhara & Mathura art.
- Satavahanas: Simuka → Pratishthana; Gautamiputra Satakarni (mother's Nasik inscription); first Brahmana land grants; lead-potin coins.
- Trade ports: Tamralipti (E), Bharuch (W), Muziris, Arikamedu (Roman finds).

patterns.name: Post-Mauryan dynasties in order and their kings
patterns.howToSpot: 'Which dynasty came after the Sungas', 'Rudradaman belonged to', ordering Sunga-Kanva-Indo-Greek-Shaka-Parthian-Kushana.
patterns.logic:
1. Heartland chain: **Sunga (185-73 BCE) → Kanva (73-28 BCE)**; NW entries in order **Indo-Greeks → Shakas → Parthians → Kushanas**.
2. King hooks: Menander = Indo-Greek; Rudradaman I = Shaka (Ujjain); Gondophernes = Parthian; Kanishka = Kushana.
3. Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription = first long chaste-Sanskrit record + Sudarshana lake repair.

example.q: Who repaired the **Sudarshana lake** and issued the first long inscription in chaste Sanskrit?
example.solution: **Rudradaman I**, the Shaka ruler of Ujjain — his Junagadh rock inscription (c. 130 CE).

patterns.name: Kushanas: Kanishka and his age
patterns.howToSpot: 'The Shaka era was started by', first gold coins, Kanishka's capitals, Gandhara vs Mathura art, scholars at his court.
patterns.logic:
1. Coin chain: Indo-Greeks = portraits; **Vima Kadphises = first gold**; Satavahanas = lead/potin; Kushanas = gold dynasty.
2. Kanishka: **78 CE = Shaka era**; capitals **Purushpura (Peshawar)** + Mathura; 4th Council; Hinayana/Mahayana split.
3. Court circle: Ashvaghosha, Charaka, Vasumitra, Nagarjuna; art: Gandhara (Greco-Buddhist) and Mathura (red sandstone).

example.q: Which Kushana ruler first issued **gold coins** in India?
example.solution: **Vima Kadphises** — Kanishka's father; Kanishka continued the gold coinage on Roman-standard weights.

patterns.name: Satavahanas: rulers, capital and social practice
patterns.howToSpot: 'Capital of the Satavahanas', Gautamiputra Satakarni's titles, first land grants, lead-potin coins, Prakrit language.
patterns.logic:
1. Founders and place: **Simuka**; capital **Pratishthana (Paithan)** on the Godavari.
2. Greatest king **Gautamiputra Satakarni** — 'destroyer of Kshatriyas'; evidence = mother **Gautami Balashri's Nasik inscription**.
3. Firsts: **first land grants to Brahmanas**; coins in **lead and potin**; language Prakrit.

example.q: The greatest Satavahana ruler, called the 'destroyer of Kshatriyas', was —
example.solution: **Gautamiputra Satakarni**, known from his mother **Gautami Balashri's** inscription at Nasik.

patterns.name: Indo-Roman trade: ports, goods, coins
patterns.howToSpot: 'Arikamedu is famous for', 'the main east-coast port', Roman gold hoards, Periplus of the Erythraean Sea.
patterns.logic:
1. Ports: **Tamralipti** (east, Ganga delta), **Bharuch/Bhrigukachchha** and Sopara (west), **Muziris** (Kerala), **Arikamedu** (Coromandel).
2. Arikamedu = arretine Roman pottery, lamps, beads — a Roman trading post.
3. Roman gold coin hoards = trade surplus for India; *Periplus of the Erythraean Sea* is the Greek sailing guide.

example.q: Which post-Mauryan coastal site in the south is famous for **Roman pottery** and trade goods?
example.solution: **Arikamedu** (near Pondicherry) — arretine ware, Roman lamps and beads prove direct Indo-Roman trade.

subtopics.title: Gupta Age & Harshavardhana
subtopics.concept:
**Gupta rulers**

| Ruler | Facts |
|---|---|
| Sri Gupta | Founder |
| Ghatotkacha | Second ruler |
| **Chandragupta I** (c. 319–335) | First *Maharajadhiraja*; married Licchavi princess **Kumaradevi**; **Gupta era 319–320 CE** |
| **Samudragupta** (c. 335–375) | **Prayag Prashasti** on the Allahabad pillar, composed by court poet **Harishena**; called **"Napoleon of India"** by V.A. Smith; *Kaviraja*; coins show him **playing the veena**; Ashvamedha; Sri Lankan king **Meghavarman** sought permission for a monastery at Bodh Gaya |
| **Chandragupta II "Vikramaditya"** (c. 375–415) | Defeated the Western Kshatrapas (Shakas); daughter **Prabhavatigupta** married Vakataka **Rudrasena II**; **Fa-Hien** visited; **Navaratnas**; **Mehrauli Iron Pillar** (rust-free; inscription of king "Chandra"); first Gupta **silver coins**; Ujjain as second capital |
| **Kumaragupta I** | Founded **Nalanda Mahavihara**; title *Mahendraditya* |
| **Skandagupta** | Repulsed the **Hunas**; repaired the **Sudarshana lake** (Junagadh inscription) |

Later: **Huna** chiefs **Toramana** and **Mihirakula**; Mihirakula was defeated by **Yashodharman** of Malwa. Gupta gold coins = **dinara**; silver = *rupaka*. **Agrahara** grants to Brahmanas.

**Navaratnas of Chandragupta II (traditional list):** **Kalidasa**, **Amarasimha** (*Amarakosha*), Dhanvantari (medicine), Vararuchi (grammar), Varahamihira (astronomy), Shanku (architecture), Kshapanaka, Vetala Bhatta, Ghatakarpara.

**Science**

| Scholar | Work | Contribution |
|---|---|---|
| **Aryabhata** (b. 476 CE, Kusumapura) | **Aryabhatiya** (499 CE) | Earth rotates on its axis; eclipses due to shadows; π ≈ 3.1416; place value — India's **first satellite (1975)** named after him |
| **Varahamihira** | *Brihat Samhita*, *Pancha Siddhantika* | Encyclopaedia of astrology, astronomy, botany |
| **Brahmagupta** | *Brahmasphuta Siddhanta* (628 CE) | Rules for operating with **zero** |
| Vagbhata | *Ashtanga Hridaya* | Medicine |

**Gupta art & architecture:** **Dashavatara temple, Deogarh** (Lalitpur, UP — early *shikhara*, panchayatana), **Bhitargaon** brick temple (Kanpur), **Udayagiri caves** (Varaha panel, Vidisha), Sarnath school of Buddha images, several **Ajanta** caves (Vakataka patronage). Gupta age called the **"Classical/Golden Age"**.

**Chinese pilgrims**

| Pilgrim | Period / ruler | Account |
|---|---|---|
| **Fa-Hien (Faxian)** | 399–414 CE, **Chandragupta II** | *Fo-kwo-ki* (Record of Buddhist Kingdoms) |
| **Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang)** | c. 630–645 CE, **Harsha** (also Pulakeshin II's Deccan, Pallava Kanchi) | ***Si-Yu-Ki***; studied at **Nalanda**; "Prince of Pilgrims" |
| **I-Tsing (Yijing)** | 671–695 CE | Studied at Nalanda |

**Harshavardhana (606–647 CE)**
- **Pushyabhuti (Vardhana)** dynasty; capital **Thanesar → Kannauj**; **Harsha era 606 CE**.
- Court poet **Banabhatta** — ***Harshacharita*** and ***Kadambari***.
- Harsha himself wrote Sanskrit plays **Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika**.
- Defeated on the **Narmada** by Chalukya **Pulakeshin II** (recorded in the **Aihole inscription** by **Ravikirti**).
- Held the **Kannauj assembly (643 CE)** honouring Hiuen Tsang and the five-yearly **Prayag assembly** (*Mahamoksha Parishad*).
